<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices with no evidence of malicious behavior. It uses a git-based source from the official upstream repository (v2editor.com) and performs standard preparation steps including LFS setup, remote addition, and version verification. The build process runs standard commands (compile, build, electron-builder) and the packaging phase copies resources and creates a desktop entry. All file operations are confined to the package's own directory ($pkgname) and related artifacts. There are no suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, unauthorized system modifications, or backdoor indicators. The sed substitution for Electron version replacement is a legitimate template processing step, and the gendesk command is a known tool for generating desktop entries in AUR projects. The entire build process is transparent and aligns with expected packaging workflows.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>

<details>

It declares the upstream source as `git+https://github.com/oktana-coop/v2.git#tag=v0.18.1`, which corresponds to the official v2 editor project on GitHub under the oktana-coop organization. This is a legitimate and expected upstream source for the package.

The only additional local file referenced is `v2.sh.in`, which is a standard template file used in packaging (commonly for generating start scripts), and its checksum is provided. No suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, encoded payloads, or unexpected file operations are present. The file operations and content are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for a source-based package.

There are no indicators of malicious behavior such as data exfiltration, execution of remote code, or tampering with unrelated system files. The checksum is provided for the local file, and no SKIP is used, which is good practice.
</details>
